title: Aria’s Last Battle
dek: A march into a war between greater powers ends in Aria’s death, the slaughter of her troops and a confrontation over Magnus’s soul.

body:
The expedition that ends with Aria’s death begins with scouts and a choice of destinations. Míriel’s tired interplanar scouts narrow the fighting to three lands: two already devastated, and a third that appears civilized and alive. The company mobilizes rather than setting out to stage Aria’s final battle.

Through the Gates and into the storm

Aria, Arandiel and Míriel prepare the troops. A trio of Gates opens and the legions march through. Beyond them lies an unsettling island: buildings stand with empty rooms and flickering edges, and the travelers catch traces of people and laughter they cannot hold in view.

The army advances inland. Adelia and Jiangshi tire during the long march. At the edge of a vast storm, after roughly nine hours of travel, the soldiers halt for orders. Going farther means crossing wind and flying debris toward a battle already underway.

A battlefield with divided allegiances

At the center, the travelers find a shattered civic space and combat between divine warriors, angels and Death’s forces. They enter a struggle whose participants exceed the boundaries of their own company and its earlier wars.

Scribonia’s meteor swarm destroys much of the remaining Heavenly Host. Talan calls for reinforcements and continues fighting. The ground begins to shake, and reality behind the company starts to fade as something approaches. The available time to act is running out.

Talan and Aria

Talan and Aria meet and lock eyes. She catches his raised weapon. Her hatred belongs to a long history of unanswered prayers and the authority she believes failed her, while he declares that Justice and Law are his being.

The fight turns against her. The narration makes clear that she is outmatched even as her troops press forward in an effort to reach their leader. Talan kills her. The final description brings Pride back to a frightened child at the feet of the monster she has tried to destroy.

Talan then leaves through the opening. The survivors are left with her body and a battle whose meaning they do not all share. Olokun’s attachment and Scribonia’s hatred of his former captor both belong to the aftermath. Neither feeling cancels what the other has experienced.

Death among the survivors

The remaining fighting subsides, but the rumbling grows louder. Dumuzi appears and ends the lives of the Zarathian troops with a flick of his hands. Magnus sees his people dead, falls to his knees and vomits.

Dumuzi invokes a soul already belonging to him, and Magnus collapses. The act demonstrates power over Magnus; it does not prove that every choice Magnus has made was commanded by Death.

Eugene uses Healing Word in an attempt to help him. Wren later shoots Magnus after he rises. He wakes in blood and vomit and tries to flee. Scribonia rejects the idea that Magnus is one of theirs, while Olokun resists treating a misguided person as someone who can simply be abandoned or killed.

The body and the departure

Dumuzi asks for Aria’s body and calls her his daughter, saying she has failed. Olokun disputes that claim to fatherhood and accuses him of using her. The exchange establishes what the two say; it does not settle the exact nature of the relationship or turn a claim of care into proof of it.

The approaching Wyrm leaves no room for an indefinite argument. The survivors must depart. A Plane Shift is confirmed to work, and Death’s departure allows the suppressed magic to return.

What her death leaves behind

Aria’s death removes an extraordinary cultural and military leader from Zarathis without erasing the civic offices beside which she acted. The later mourning, judgments and conflicts over her legacy grow from this loss. They also carry the lives she harmed and the people who loved her.

A much later claim by Dumuzi that Aria is not dead belongs to the Babel encounter. It is linked as later testimony, not used to erase this witnessed killing or supply an unseen resurrection.

People and places in this history Aria / Pride · Magnus Niriin · Olokun · Scribonia · Wren · Eugene · Zarathis · authority after Aria
